public_notes.title: Land, Work And Community
public_notes.text: The Tribe locates its community in southern Alabama and connects the name MOWA with Mobile and Washington Counties. Its land history describes how logging in the late 1800s displaced families while providing work. It describes loss of land through debts or unpaid taxes, and families cooperating to move logs to market. These are the Tribe's historical accounts of livelihood and land, not a finding about any present property's ownership.

public_notes.title: Education And Self-Definition
public_notes.text: The Tribe's Social Barriers chapter recounts exclusion from schools and parents taking their children's access to court. It dates a school-aid request to 1934. The same chapter challenges outsiders' descriptions that obscured the community's Choctaw identity. This is the Tribe's retrospective account; discriminatory language quoted from older publications is evidence of exclusion, not terminology adopted by this profile.
